title: America’s Climate Free Fall
author: Robert Hunziker
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/getty-
images-5HTSTyX7CfA-unsplash-680x510.jpg)

Image by Getty and Unsplash+.

Climate tipping points are critical thresholds that trigger unstoppable shifts
to another state. The global climate system is full of teetering tipping
points that collectively threaten the climate system with radical change. But
it’s the change itself, the transition to a tipping point, that is most
chaotic. This is climate free fall in America today, dangerously exposing the
country to risks overlooked by policy decision-makers.

Climate free fall has been identified by Anders Kevernann, Potsdam Institute
for Climate Impact Research, Germany, Professor of the Dynamics of the Climate
System at Institute for Physics and Astrophysics: “The planet is heading for
climate free fall, a period where increasingly erratic weather will stress
global supply chains, spike insurance losses, and undermine the financial
stability modern economies depend on. The greatest economic risks lie not at
the endpoint of climate change, but in how we get there.” (_Climate Free Fall:
Scientists Warn of Hidden Economic Crisis, Earth’s Systems Become Dangerously
Unstable_ , [Earth Climate](https://earthclimate.eu/2026/07/18/climate-free-
fall-scientists-warn-of-hidden-economic-crisis-earths-systems-become-
dangerously-
unstable/?fbclid=IwY2xjawTKDmBleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFKWkhmTWlUOFlyenIzRUxvc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHuzxiBRPMt2OAk1pRjR_LtE_KJw6JtUQrHD4e4luB2bbvtXs8tpmLBXfQTxg_aem_ixCuDqjxzMaO_7rfoalF1A),
July 18, 2026)

**America’s Climate Free Fall**

America is already experiencing a chaotic climate system that’s effectively
climate free fall.

As of July 14, 2026, 46.47% of the Lower States are in drought. (Source:
Drought.gov and National Centers for Environmental Information). Drought in
the Lower States is an astonishing 40% worse than the ~33% drought index for
the world which itself is triple the global drought index of 10-12% in the
year 2000.

Nearly one-third (1/3rd) of the planet is afflicted with
[drought](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43017-026-00785-z) as climate
change-driven heat pulls moisture from soils and plants at unprecedented
rates.

Flash floods- The National Weather Service issued double the number of flash
flood warnings, totaling 3,600 in 2025, versus the year 2000: “The dramatic
escalation in flash flooding over the last quarter-century is driven by a
warming atmosphere holding more moisture, resulting in extreme, high-intensity
thunderstorms,” because too much fossil fuel CO2 brings too much atmospheric
heat.

Capitalism measures success and failure in dollars, to wit: In 2025 the US
experienced “twenty-three (23) billion-dollar weather disasters” at a total
cost of $115 billion. In the year 2000 there were “three (3) billion-dollar
disasters.” The year 2025 included a record-setting number of (1) severe
storms (2) hail events (3) tornadoes. This is climate free fall on steroids.
(Trump has discontinued the government’s tracking of billion-dollar climate
disasters. The public doesn’t need to know how much damage is caused by
climate change.)

Monetary matters have become a key factor with climate change. It’s well
documented that major home insurers in America have been fleeing coastal
states and/or raising rates or dropping coverage for homeowners due to a whole
new slate of climate risks, like unprecedented massive wildfires in California
and Oklahoma and Utah and Alaska and Nebraska and Colorado and Florida,
examples of chaotic climate change at severe levels never previously
experienced in American history. This climate juggernaut increasingly
threatens several aspects of American life.

“There is a growing body of research connecting extreme weather, exacerbated
by climate change, to insurance price increases. A US Treasury Department
analysis of more that 243 million home policies, released in January 2025,
[concluded](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-
releases/jy2791?utm_source=chatgpt.com) that communities routinely affected by
severe weather were paying substantially more than those that were not.” (_US
Home Insurance Prices Set to Keep Rising with Severe Weather_ , Bloomberg,
March 18, 2026)

And this headline in the DC Report d/d July 19, 2026, says it all: “An Extreme
Heat Wave: The Hottest Temperatures in History Occurring All Over the
Country.” Meteorologist and Director of Climate Matters, Bernadette Woods
Placky, told CNN, “Earth is screaming at us right now and people need to
listen.”

But America’s energy policies, ignoring the US Treasury analysis and not
listening to Bernadette, favor fossil fuels oil, gas, coal that emit gigatons
of CO2 largely responsible for climate free fall, to wit: “Carbon dioxide
(CO2) is the single largest driver of the erratic and extreme weather changes
in the U.S. By trapping heat in the atmosphere, elevated (CO2) alters global
atmospheric circulation and disrupts historical weather patterns.” (Source:
NOAA - National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration)

**What Happens if Climate Free Fall Gets Worse, Not Better?**

Alas, America is blindly cranking up climate free fall by destroying clean
energy sources in favor of filthy, harmful fossil fuels, like coal. If climate
free fall gets worse, the listed consequences above will be small shadows of
the above-listed scenarios. How else interpret the administration’s policy
behavior? See more about this growing tragedy for the country further on in
this text.

“[Tipping points](https://earthclimate.eu/?s=Tipping%20points) in climate
science are well-defined: they occur when a series of interlinked changes
amplify one another until the whole system becomes unstable and shifts
uncontrollably into a different state. Loss of [sea
ice](https://earthclimate.eu/?s=sea%20ice) at the poles, for example, reduces
the amount of sunlight reflected into space, further heating Earth’s surface,
which then accelerates ice loss—a vicious cycle that defines the tipping
process.” (Anders Kevernann)

Climate free fall instability is already evident throughout the world, for
example, roughly [33% of global land surface is in
drought](https://coveringclimatenow.org/from-us-story/as-global-drought-
deepens-climate-change-kills-by-a-thousand-cuts/) versus 10-12% in 2000.
That’s a tripling of average global drought in only 25 years. This is
worldwide climate free fall in earnest. Hence, the economic impact for food
production and habitability is threatened well before exceeding tipping
points.

The highest risk periods for the world economic systems occur during the big
transition period to tipping points: “The period between passing the tipping
temperature and reaching the full tipping point—when system collapse becomes
inevitable—is when [weather
fluctuations](https://earthclimate.eu/?s=weather%20fluctuations) increase most
dramatically. This transition could unfold over decades, creating a prolonged
period of [economic
disruption](https://earthclimate.eu/?s=economic%20disruption).” (Anders
Kevernann)

Tipping points are triggered by “temperatures” beyond pre-industrial. For
example, ‘temperature trigger points’ for key ecosystems, [Source:
](https://www.fortomorrow.eu/en/blog/tipping-point/)Potsdam Institute for
Climate Impact Research: (1) Greenland Ice Sheet triggers at 1.5C (2) Arctic
Winter Sea Ice 4.5C (3) Boreal Permafrost 4C (4) West Antarctic Ice Sheet 1.5C
(5) East Antarctic Ice Sheet 7.5C (6) East Antarctica Subglacial Basins 3C,
(7) AMOC 4C (8) Labrador-Irminger Sea Convection 1.8C (9) Amazon Rainforest
3.5C.

As outlined, some of the most vulnerable, most impactful climate systems are
already knocking on the door. The consequences for sea level rise could be
devastating, catching society unaware, unprepared.

**Clean Energy Darkness and Absurd Threats to Society**

“Trump administration policies that scaled back federal support for clean
energy have led to the cancellation ​or delay of $83 billion in investment
across hundreds of projects, according to a report ‌released on Tuesday by
labor and environmental coalition BlueGreen Alliance. The analysis found that
223 manufacturing and clean energy projects representing $82.9 ​billion in
investment and 111,765 jobs have stalled or been cancelled during President
Donald Trump's ​second presidency.” (_Trump Cut to Clean Energy Linked to $83
Billion in Delayed or Canceled Projects_ ,
[Reuters,](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/trump-clean-energy-
policies-linked-83-billion-delayed-or-canceled-projects-2026-07-14/) July 16,
2026)

Additionally, according to [Sierra](https://www.sierraclub.org/sierra/us-
faces-triple-threat-climate-crisis-economic-hardship-and-donald-trump) d/d
June 14, 2026: _US Faces Triple Threat of Climate Crisis, Economic Hardship,
and Donald Trump_ : “In addition to staffing and budget cuts at NOAA—affecting
offices like the National Weather Service and the National Hurricane
Center—the administration has targeted satellite infrastructure and data used
for weather and [hurricane forecasting](https://apnews.com/article/climate-
hurricane-forecasting-weather-defense-satellites-
ea4cdb91c891255add2e9a94c28606ef), scrapped the scientists working on the next
National Climate Assessment, and discontinued the government’s tracking of
billion-dollar climate disasters. It has also taken aim at [the National
Center for Atmospheric Research](https://ncar.ucar.edu/), considered ‘the
crown jewel’ of climate science.”

The National Center for Atmospheric Research
(“[NCAR](https://blogs.edf.org/climate411/2026/03/11/why-dismantling-the-
nations-atmospheric-research-backbone-would-be-a-costly-mistake/)”) is the
“primary go-to source” for international science. NCAR serves (1) actuaries
and reinsurers (2) the aviation industry (3) emergency managers (4) utilities
and power grid planners (5) as well as thousands of scientists in diverse
fields internationally. It’s world renown for cutting-edge statistics. **The
entire world of science and business depends upon its accuracy.** Any level of
loss of NCAR would be considered an international tragedy.

“With disaster preparedness and response, experts say the administration has
severely undermined [the Federal Emergency Management
Authority](https://www.fema.gov/) through deep staffing and budget cuts,
delays on aid delivery and even politicization of disaster response. Trump’s
proposed FY 2027 budget includes
[axing](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-fy27-budget-slashes-
climate-100934303.html?guccounter=1) $1.3 billion in FEMA funds for state and
local emergency preparedness. And [according to Climate
Power](https://climatepower.us/news/on-the-first-day-of-hurricane-season-
trump-has-left-us-unprepared/), the US is entering this hurricane season with
the smallest disaster workforce since 2021,” Ibid.

“Climate free fall” lands with a thud at the feet of an ill-prepared,
dumbfounded Trump administration.
